title: Abort-machine characterization of zero-error computation
statement: Let $L$ be a language of bit strings. If there are a natural number $c$ and a finite nondeterministic Turing machine whose running time on inputs of length $n$ is bounded by $a(n^c+1)$ for some natural number $a$, such that every length-matched choice string makes the machine halt, its output is never the one-bit indicator of membership in $L$, and that output equals the indicator with probability at least $1/2$ under uniformly random choices, then $L$ has an efficient polynomial-witness verifier with no incorrect answers and probability at most $1/2$ of giving no answer.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language of bit strings
$L$ belongs to the class defined as the union over natural $c$ of languages decided by an aborting probabilistic Turing machine
There is a natural number $a$ and a finite nondeterministic Turing machine witnessing that membership
The machine halts on every choice string of the prescribed input-dependent length
For every such choice string, the output differs from the one-bit membership indicator
The probability of outputting the membership indicator is at least $1/2$
